newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia sees '96/97 817.9 bln rph budget surplus.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia sees '96/97 817.9 bln rph budget surplus.

text.p: Indonesian Finance Minister Mar'ie Muhammad said on Tuesday the country's 1996/97 (April-March) budget will have a surplus of 817.9 bln rupiah.
He told a parliamentary hearing the 1996/97 budget revenue would be at 95.840 trillion rupiah and spending will be at 95.022 trillion.
Mar'ie also predicted that the price of crude oil would average $20.76 per barrel during the fiscal year ending March 31 against the targetted price of $16.50 per barrel.

"The 1996/97 budget needs to be changed, because revenue is estimated at 95.840 trillion rupiah and spending at 95.022 trillion rupiah. So in the 1996/97 budget we have a surplus of 817.9 billion rupiah," Mar'ie said in a statement.
"Total exports in 1996/97 are estimated to rise 10 percent to $52.6 billion. The current account deficit will be $8.8 billion."
Mar'ie said imports and services will be at $61.4 billion in the 1996/97 budget.
He also predicted the country's inflation will be around an average of six percent in the budget.
He said Indonesia's inflation was 6.47 percent in calendar 1996 against 8.64 percent in 1995.
